_README: One row per (edition PDF, page). The window is stated as reference measure
NUMBERS, never as a count, because the corpus uses both anacrusis
conventions: Mahler 5 numbers its pickup 0, Bach BWV1048 numbers its pickup
1 (so the reference runs +1 against the print), and everything else starts
at a full bar numbered 1. `first_ref_measure`/`last_ref_measure` go straight
to music21's Stream.measures(a, b), which matches NUMBERS and is INCLUSIVE.
`confidence` is load-bearing. scan_eval.py REFUSES to report a pooled figure
while any scored row is `first_pass`: a pooled number over an unverified
window is the 0.8706-against-seventeen-measures mistake with more decimals.
`staves` maps each PRINTED staff to the reference part indices it carries,
and its clef/key are HAND-READ OFF THE SCAN — the page is the truth, not the
file. It is optional; without it the row reports OMR-NED only.
Paths are relative to the score library (tools.library.score_library
.library_root(), which resolves to the MAIN checkout from a worktree).

protocol.why_no_dossier: data/dossiers/ is generated from the same Gradus MusicXML used here as truth, so --dossier would hand the run its own answer key

rows.label: Beethoven 5 / Litolff-family / low-res bitonal

window.established_by: probe_page_measures.py — five tacet staves (Flauti, Oboi, Corni, Trombe, Timpani), full-height columns that continue past the staff into the gap; all five give 16
window.verified_by: 2026-08-31, corrected from a wrong 17 that all five staves agreed on because all five print the same time signature

rows.notes: The window and the staves map are the first run's, reused verbatim so this row is a controlled reproduction. The print gives Trombe and Timpani NO key signature where the Gradus file gives them three flats; the page wins.

rows.label: Beethoven 5 / same plates, high-res + text layer

window.established_by: same printed page as row 1 (identical 12-staff layout, part names, meter and key signatures), independently re-counted from the tacet Flauti staff

rows.notes: Same music and same window as row 1; what differs is scan resolution AND the text layer together. The text layer turns on staff_labels.read_staff_labels, which feeds part naming and contextual clef filling, and a filled clef does reach OMR-NED — so this is not a pure resolution A/B. 575951 also carries modern English running heads (`2 SYMPHONY NO. 5 (1)`) that 984073 does not: a later reprint of the same plates, catalogued with identical provenance.

rows.label: Dvorak 9 / Simrock 1894 / the one 1:1 part-staff pair

window.established_by: tacet `Trombe in E` staff — whole-bar rests counted visually at 250 dpi

rows.notes: The only work in the library whose printed staff count equals its reference part count, and in the same order. No condensation, so no `entire staff insert/delete` floor — the row where OMR-NED measures recognition rather than the export's part model. PDF index 2 is a Contents page for a two-symphony volume with Symphony 8 struck through; index 3 is blank. Clefs/keys not yet hand-read.

rows.label: Brahms 1 / Breitkopf Samtliche Werke / dense, engraved twin

edition.raster: ~5276x6940 ccitt bitonal @~533ppi (dimensions vary per page), page 711.6x936.3 pt

window.established_by: tacet `2 Trompeten in C` staff (m1 has notes, then six whole-bar rests) with the Pauken staff agreeing
window.cross_check: the system ends with a CAUTIONARY 9/8 printed after the final barline, and the reference changes meter to 9/8 at measure 8. The page therefore ends at m7 — a fact from the reference, with no failure mode shared with counting ink.

rows.notes: Same music as brahms-sym1-mvt1 in benchmarks/omr-orchestral-e2e — the engraved-vs-scan delta on identical notes. Clefs/keys not yet hand-read.

rows.label: Mahler 5 / Edition Peters / densest, anacrusis

edition.publisher_as_catalogued: (unidentified scan 2016); the page itself says Edition Peters No. 3087b

window.established_by: tacet `Vier Floten` staff — a quarter rest before the first barline (the pickup, reference measure 0, ql 1.0) then whole-bar rests

rows.notes: PDF index 0 is the Peters title page; a horizontal-rule probe called it music because of the decorative frame. Reference measure 0 has ql 1.0 and paddingLeft 3.0 — the solo trumpet upbeat, and the printed page shows exactly that. Staff count not yet established (the percussion block is tightly spaced). Same music as mahler-sym5-mvt1 in the engraved benchmark.

rows.label: Bach Brandenburg 3 / Edition Peters / 300 dpi, +1 numbering

window.established_by: system 1 = a narrow pickup cell (two sixteenths) plus 4 full bars, confirmed by the boxed `5` opening the next block. Reference numbers the PICKUP measure 1, so system 1 is reference mm. 1-5.

rows.notes: NOT RUNNABLE until last_ref_measure is established. The page shows three blocks — full score, then a strings block and a Cembalo block BOTH carrying the boxed 5 — so the system structure is itself an open question. Kept as a stress row: it is the only work whose reference numbering runs +1 against the print.
